engagement_background.objective: SaVida Health engaged Treya Partners to generate approximately $240K–$470K in cost savings through strategic sourcing across multiple spend categories, while maintaining or improving service levels and leveraging the company’s enterprise-wide purchasing power within a six-month project window (quick wins by end of 2024 and full completion by March 2025).
engagement_background.scope_summary: Initial scope covers 10 indirect and clinical-support spend categories (EMR, Employee Benefits, Scientific/Medical Lab Equipment & Supplies, Medical Equipment & Supplies, Small Parcel, IT Hardware, Telecom, Office Supplies, Commercial Print, Waste Management) representing a $5.3 M baseline. Up to 90 % of this spend is addressable, but low-opportunity categories may be dropped or re-categorised as better data emerges.
constraints_challenges: Supplier non-responsiveness to data requests, delaying baseline creation and RFx work.
Need for a unified, ‘no side conversations’ communication strategy to prevent supplier pushback.
Potential lack of stakeholder availability for data provision, interviews, and timely feedback.
Pressure to realise quick-hit savings before year-end and finish the full programme by mid-March 2025.
Incumbent supplier sensitivities during competitive bidding or renegotiations.
Gaps in line-item usage data, requiring supplier outreach and acceptance of representative samples.
Requirement for SaVida to cease parallel procurement activity in in-scope categories to avoid market confusion.

procurement_environment.data_availability: Internal AP/PO data exists but is insufficient at the line-item level; current contracts are scattered and supplier usage reports are not consistently received, so Treya must obtain detailed data directly from key vendors.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: No single contract repository; multiple suppliers per category; historical usage data often incomplete, requiring representative sampling after six weeks of collection effort if gaps remain.
